review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–119). I also grepped the sibling Hilbert files, for example Triv.lean, for the same pattern. The only repetition is the two-line block `unfold ReflexiveEuclideanFrameClass MultiGeacheanConfluentFrameClass MultiGeachean; simp [Geachean.reflexive_def, Geachean.euclidean_def]`. It appears in both `S5.Kripke.sound` and `S5.Kripke.complete`, next to a `convert ... (G := {⟨0,0,1,0⟩, ⟨1,1,0,1⟩})` call. This is routine unfolding plus `simp`, not substantial mathematical reasoning. Factoring it into a lemma saying the class equals the Geach class would only move a short duplicated branch into a helper, which the rubric says is not enough. I did not run Lean, so I could not check how `simp` behaves on that goal. `soundUniversal` and `completeUniversal` are thin wrappers around `iff_validOnUniversalFrameClass_validOnReflexiveEuclideanFrameClass` and the existing soundness and completeness instances. The remaining proofs, the point-generated argument and the frame-class equality, each occur once. I found no justified repeated-proof-machinery finding.
